name: jefscad
//: Read the comment in .devcontainer/Dockerfile first. Containment here is a function of what is NOT mounted and NOT installed, so the mount list below is deliberately short. Before adding a mount, ask: does this need to be writable, does it carry a credential, and is there a path that does not require it? Every mount is a hole in the boundary.
//mounts-why: Six mounts, and each earns its place. (1) the repo-scoped PAT, at the same relative path it has on the host so git-askpass.sh needs no container-specific variant. NOT the ~/.config/jef directory — that would also expose the pixel-world and termcanvas PATs. (2) and (3) the shared instruction files, read-only so the agent cannot edit the rules it is operating under. (4) the wiki, read-only: full read access to all three tiers — including projects/flint, which this project depends on for interval arithmetic, so the cross-project architectural reading is real here — and no ability to write, because the wiki is the one tier where an undetected error compounds instead of being caught. Updates go to notes/wiki-proposals/ and a human promotes them. (5) ~/.msmtprc, for the unsupervised summary email. This is the one mount that exists purely for a notification, so it is worth being explicit about the trade: it hands the container the ability to send mail as the user. It is read-only and the agent is instructed to send exactly one message per run, to jefwagner@gmail.com, never to anyone else. If that is not acceptable, drop this mount and the email instruction together — the fallback is a summary file in the branch, as pixel-world does. (6) pi-auth.json, mounted directly at ~/.pi/agent/auth.json — the exact path pi reads — so the OpenRouter API key is available to the pi coding agent with no container-specific config. Like the PAT it is a single file rather than the whole ~/.config/jef directory, and read-only so an agent cannot overwrite or replace its own credential. The read-only mount means /login inside the container cannot persist a new credential; rotating the token means editing ~/.config/jef/pi-auth.json on the host and rebuilding the container. NOT ~/.ssh (the personal key reaches every repo on the account, including the wiki), NOT ~/.config/lab-bot, NOT ~/.aws or ~/.azure, NOT the host tool directory, NOT the docker socket (maturin builds the extension in-process; no container runtime is needed here).

remoteEnv.//git: GIT_ASKPASS points at the tracked script that reads the mounted PAT. GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 stops a failed lookup from falling back to an interactive prompt, which in an unattended run hangs until the run is killed. GIT_SSH_COMMAND=/bin/false is a second line of defence behind the missing ssh binary: even if one is added later, git cannot silently fall back to SSH.
